source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Leaf spot disease (ជម្ងឺអុចស្លឹកពោត, also called ព្រុកចាប): this is a fungal disease observed on corn leaves. Symptoms appear as roundish spots with an old-brown colored center and a surrounding yellowish-tan halo/ring. The disease spreads across the leaf surface, caused by fungal spores. It spreads from plant to plant, or from one field to another, via irrigation water, tools and equipment, transport, and various human field activities. Conditions that favor this disease's development are warm temperatures combined with high atmospheric humidity.

Prevention and control measures:
- Plant according to the appropriate season/timing.
- Keep the field clean.
- Collect and burn crop debris/residue showing disease symptoms, and use clean seed before planting.
